notes: Uses closure_statement_date, the same no-rule-consumes field/value as EV-ABST-001 (abstention suite), deliberately NOT R01/R02's fields. Two live runs against real Postgres showed those originally-chosen fields (full_repayment_date/original_docs_released_date) don't give a deterministic rollup: R01 AND R02 both consume them (so 2 rules fire, not 1 -- a case-design mistake), and both currently run in shadow mode since every corpus instrument is still verification_status=unverified (CLAUDE.md-mandated: no citable verdict without a resolvable citation against verified law), so their violations are correctly excluded from loan_compliance_state's counts by app/verdict/state.py -- and because no rule is ever 'decided' while shadow, assess_fact ALSO calls the model per field, and its real-LLM verdict (ambiguous vs no_clause_found) varied between the two live runs, changing highest_severity via app/verdict/severity.py's FIELD_SEVERITY_DEFAULT[CLOSURE]. See ADR-052's follow-up correction. This case sidesteps all of that: no rule consumes closure_statement_date at all, so there is exactly one assess_fact call and one model verdict, inheriting the same abstention_correctness reliability already measured by the abstention suite (0.825 live) rather than a new, compounded source of flakiness.
